Element.attribute: Document a plan that will allow the organization to dismiss or stop the process to transition a solution into production, if a decision not to proceed is made prior to the start of the cutover and deployment.

Element.Name: define_contingency_plan,_L7TTADHGEe-ymZgH1AiGoQ
Element.attribute: The contingency plan establishes how to delay a go-live date or how to proceed with limited functionality or restricted scope. Its main goal is to maintain a minimum level of service and business functionality, or to revert to the previous environment.

A contingency plan is required in the event that cutover issues cannot be resolved in a timely manner and business may suffer as a result. The plan must address how long (in hours or days) the new production system may be in operation before it is no longer possible to roll back to the legacy systems. It is standard practice to have a point of no return for making the new system operative.

Include contingency plans in standard operating procedures. Make sure initial training is provided on the plan. 

Keep the plan current and everyone up-to-date on changes.

Manage risk; look for opportunities to reduce risk wherever possible. This may help reduce, or even eliminate, the need for full contingency plans in certain areas.

Consider resource restrictions. Will the organization be able to function the same way if you have to implement Plan B, or will Plan B necessarily reduce capabilities?
To define the activities required for the organization to be able to quickly respond if plans for a solution cutover into product cannot go forward.
